tldr_label: TL;DR — Eisenkot starts coalition talks, Abu Dhabi peace talks open Tuesday, and the House may vote to impeach Hegseth

tldr_bullets.label: Israel
tldr_bullets.body: Eisenkot formally received the mandate and opened coalition talks. Liberman rejects a minority government that relies on Arab parties. [[TAG:info:28 days]]

tldr_bullets.label: Ukraine
tldr_bullets.body: Russian strikes cut power to hundreds of thousands of people before US-brokered talks in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday and Wednesday, which European officials will attend. [[TAG:danger:power cuts]]

tldr_bullets.label: US
tldr_bullets.body: Axios reports that the House is poised to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth this week. Democrats lead the uncalled Senate races in Alaska and Mississippi.

tldr_bullets.label: Iran
tldr_bullets.body: Trump says new attacks are 'highly unlikely' if Tehran agrees a nuclear deal and reopens Hormuz. Israel's defense minister says the 'mission is not complete'.

tldr_bullets.label: Markets
tldr_bullets.body: Asian stocks rebounded and Brent eased toward $97. China's factory-gate inflation hit 5.7%, its highest in more than four years.

tldr_bullets.label: Africa
tldr_bullets.body: The ANC won about 30.8% in South Africa's local polls, its worst result. A migrant boat sank off Senegal, killing between 21 and 34 people. [[TAG:warning:ANC 30.8%]]

sections.title: Eisenkot's Coalition Math
sections.summary: Eisenkot receives the mandate and sets four conditions; Liberman rejects a minority government

paragraphs.heading: Mandate
paragraphs.body: The Jerusalem Post and the Times of Israel reported that Eisenkot formally received the mandate from President Herzog on Sunday. The Times of Israel said he promised a 'creative and unconventional' path to an emergency coalition. He has 28 days, with a possible 14-day extension. [[TAG:info:clock running]]

paragraphs.heading: Conditions and obstacles
paragraphs.body: The JTA explained Eisenkot's four conditions: a Jewish and democratic state, the values of the Declaration of Independence, military service for all, and recognizing Hamas as a terrorist group. Ynet reported that Liberman rejects a minority government. The Times of Israel said Eisenkot is holding firm on mandatory service after Liberman opened the door to ultra-Orthodox parties. [[TAG:warning:deadlock risk]]

sections.title: Iran
sections.summary: Trump calls new attacks 'highly unlikely' if a deal is reached; Israel says its mission isn't done

paragraphs.heading: Signals
paragraphs.body: Fox News reported that Trump said fresh attacks on Iran are 'highly unlikely' if Tehran agrees a nuclear deal and reopens Hormuz, though the Wall Street Journal reported that his advisers are divided. CBS News said Iran played down the new US task force targeting its land routes. Asharq Al-Awsat and Arab News reported that Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz said 'the mission is not complete' and accused Iran of renewing its nuclear efforts, which Iran denies. [[TAG:warning:mixed signals]]

sections.title: Ukraine Before Abu Dhabi
sections.summary: Russian strikes black out swaths of Ukraine as Europe joins talks Moscow tried to exclude

paragraphs.heading: Blackouts
paragraphs.body: Al Jazeera and CBS News reported that Russian strikes left hundreds of thousands without power, mainly in Dnipropetrovsk and Kharkiv regions. CBC said Russia kept hitting power facilities around Kyiv as temperatures drop. Zelensky says Moscow is escalating to gain leverage before the talks. [[TAG:danger:850K without power]]

paragraphs.heading: Talks
paragraphs.body: NPR reported that European officials will join the US-brokered talks in Abu Dhabi, defying the Kremlin's objections. Yahoo News said the US, Russia and Ukraine will meet there on Tuesday and Wednesday, and WVTM said the talks will focus on security guarantees. Experts do not expect a breakthrough.

sections.title: Washington
sections.summary: House eyes impeaching Hegseth; Democrats lead the two uncalled Senate races

paragraphs.heading: Hegseth
paragraphs.body: Axios reported that the House is poised to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth after the Republican midterm defeat, in a vote forced by Republican Thomas Massie. NBC News said Hakeem Jeffries is a 'hard yes'. CNN reported that Trump defended Hegseth. Removal would require two-thirds of the Senate, which is considered unlikely. [[TAG:warning:impeachment vote]]

paragraphs.heading: Senate count
paragraphs.body: Democracy Now reported that Democrats lead in both Alaska and Mississippi. Al Jazeera explained why the calls are delayed: Mississippi must finish its count by November 13, and Alaska's ranked-choice results come on November 18. Winning both would give Democrats 56 seats.

sections.title: Markets and Economies
sections.summary: Asia rebounds and oil eases; China's factory-gate inflation hits a four-year high

paragraphs.heading: Markets
paragraphs.body: Reuters, via Investing.com, reported that Asian stocks steadied as worries about AI and the Middle East eased, while the dollar held firm on bets of a Fed hike. CNBC said US futures moved as investors brace for more data and earnings. Grafa reported that Brent fell about 1.5% toward $97, and Invezz said prices are falling despite attacks near Hormuz. US CPI is due Tuesday. [[TAG:info:CPI Tuesday]]

paragraphs.heading: China
paragraphs.body: CNBC reported that China's producer prices rose 5.7% in October, the fastest in more than four years, while consumer inflation slowed to 0.7%. Investinglive noted that the CPI figure came in below the 0.8% forecast.

paragraphs.heading: France
paragraphs.body: US News reported that Prime Minister Lecornu is holding talks with unions and employers on the cost of living after mass protests. Franceinfo said public-sector unions have called a strike for November 17.

sections.title: Africa
sections.summary: ANC's worst-ever result at about 30.8%; migrant boat disaster off Senegal

paragraphs.heading: South Africa
paragraphs.body: The Citizen reported that the ANC topped the local elections with 30.76% as President Ramaphosa warned parties ahead of coalition talks. Stuff and Anadolu called it the party's worst-ever result, down from about 45.6% in 2021. allAfrica said the DA came second with about 24.6%. Most councils have no outright majority. [[TAG:warning:ANC 30.8%]]

paragraphs.heading: Senegal
paragraphs.body: Euronews and TRT World reported at least 21 dead after a migrant boat capsized off Kebemer, citing the interior ministry. 3News and The Courier, citing the state news agency, put the toll at 34. Officials have not said how many people were aboard. [[TAG:danger:21 to 34 dead]]
